summary: Backend-only check of the ExtraPe '+' (encoded space) fix on the PREVIEW URL only. 5/5 pytest cases pass, using 9 real ExtraPe conversions. (1) Myntra with '+': https://www.myntra.com/men-tshirts?f=Brand%3ALee+Cooper&sort=new -> https://myntr.in/cexUdp. The code has no '+', ':' or '|'. It returns 302 to myntra.com/men-tshirts?f=Brand%3ALee%20Cooper&sort=new&... (2) Ajio with '+' -> https://ajiio.co/r4oH1d. This returns 302 to the ajiotrk.vibconnect.in tracker, and its url param decodes to https://www.ajio.com/men-jeans/c/830216013?query=%3Arelevance%3Abrand%3ALee%20Cooper%3Agenderfilter%3AMen&. Following the tracker lands on ajio.com with the full query intact. The final ajio.com 403 is Ajio blocking bots, not an app bug. (3) Regressions: Flipkart iPhone -> https://fkrt.co/cqnGPM (302 to dl.flipkart.com with affid). Plain Myntra ?sort=new -> https://myntr.in/5qhH60, which redirects with sort=new. (4) POST /convert/bulk with all 4 links -> all changed=true, no errors and no broken short links (myntr.in/uYZuPn, ajiio.co/vDP85A, fkrt.co/bHflLx, myntr.in/2SSA3p). All 4 redirect correctly and save_error is null.
action_items: Deploy the fix to production, then re-convert the 18 broken live myntr.in/ajiio.co deals: POST /api/public/deals/reconvert, or bulk convert their clean_url. Find them with affiliate_url matching (ajiio.co|myntr.in)/\w+[+:&].
critical_code_review_comments: engine.server.ts convertWithExtraPe: the whole query (including & and =) is encodeURIComponent'd when it contains + or %20. This relies on ExtraPe decoding exactly once. It is verified working today, but it is fragile if ExtraPe changes its behaviour. The broken-link guard is the safety net.

The broken-link guard (/[+:|]/ on any candidate whose host is not the store's) would also reject a valid long affiliate URL on another host that has a raw '+', ':' or '|' in its query, e.g. a tracker. ExtraPe returns short links today, so there is no impact now. A safer guard would only check the path or query of known shorteners (myntr.in, ajiio.co, fkrt.co, ...).
Queries that hold a literal encoded plus (%2B) are left alone, which is correct. Encoded-space detection only checks the query string, not the path. That is fine for the reported cases.
